item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Uncertainty Hangs Over Talks as U.S. Says It Is Close to Agreement
item.description: An emerging “memorandum of understanding,” which could lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, still needs approval from President Trump, and Iran has not confirmed any commitments.

item.title: Middle East war live: Israeli strikes put Lebanon's heritage sites in 'serious danger', Beirut says
item.description: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon are putting heritage sites in “serious danger”, warned Beirut's Minister of Culture Ghassan Salamé. "Bombings fell very close to the ruins of Tyre," he said, while adding that the Beaufort Castle was “directly hit”. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: A Draft U.S.-Iran Plan Is Said to Be on the Table. Here’s What to Know.
item.description: U.S. and Iranian officials say they are closing in on the terms of a preliminary agreement. Yet sticking points, particularly over the Strait of Hormuz, remain.

item.title: Hamas struggles to fill leadership ranks as Israel hunts Oct 7 terrorists
item.description: Hours after an Israeli airstrike killed Hamas military wing chief Mohammed Odeh, Gaza's Eid markets were full, revealing a disconnect with Hamas.

item.title: Closer to war or to peace? US, Iran near deal on 60-day ceasefire
item.description: The ​United States threatened Thursday to target ally Oman if it helped impose a tolling system in the key Strait of Hormuz, warning of sanctions against all parties involved in such actions. The United States and Iran also accused each other of violating an ongoing truce following an exchange of fire, three months after the Middle East war began with a wave of US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic. The latest exchange was the most serious since Washington and Tehran agreed to a ceasefire

item.title: How far have the US and Iran got towards ending the Iran war?
item.description: The United States and Iran have reached ⁠an agreement to extend ​a ceasefire, allow shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and lift a US blockade and some sanctions on Iran, sources told Reuters, but the deal has not been finalised. An agreement would represent a big step towards ending a ​war that has pushed the world towards an energy crisis, though the underlying dispute over Iran's nuclear programme would only be thrashed out in talks over subsequent weeks.

item.title: Netanyahu Says Israel Will Control 70 Percent of Gaza, Squeezing Hamas
item.description: Israel’s military continues to conduct strikes and seize territory despite a cease-fire with Hamas. Many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s supporters see the war as unfinished business.

item.title: U.S. and Iran Move Toward Agreement to Reopen the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Trump has yet to sign off on an extension of the cease-fire that would allow the two sides to negotiate nuclear and other issues.

item.title: US and Iranian Negotiators Close in on Preliminary Peace Deal
item.description: After several days of renewed strikes on both sides, the United States and Iran are closing in on a preliminary agreement that extends the ceasefire for 60 days, begins negotiations on Iran’s nuclear program and opens the Strait of Hormuz. NBC’s Richard Engel reports for TODAY.

item.title: Netanyahu directs Israeli forces to expand Gaza control to 70 percent
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday he had directed Israel's military to take more of Gaza, initially by seizing 70% of the Palestinian territory, where the population is already penned into a tiny strip of land along the coast. Israel effectively controls an estimated 64% of the tiny coastal ​Strip, bombarded to ‌ruins by Israel's two-year military assault that followed the 2023 Hamas attack on southern Israel.
